subject: Oceanography
title: Seagrass Decline
description: Learn Seagrass Decline in one minute.

hook.text: Seagrass meadows are vanishing at 7% per year—faster than tropical rainforests.

buildup.text: Seagrasses stabilize sediment, store carbon, and provide habitat for seahorses, dugongs, and juvenile fish.

discovery.text: A single hectare of seagrass produces 100,000 liters of oxygen per day—more than the same area of rainforest.

twist.text: Nutrient pollution clouds the water—blocking the sunlight seagrasses need to survive.

climax.text: 29% of global seagrass has disappeared since 1879—mainly from coastal development and water quality decline.

punchline.text: Underwater meadows outproduce rainforests—and vanish faster.

quiz.question: What is the main threat to seagrass meadows?
options: Nutrient pollution that clouds the water, blocking sunlight
